lesson.menu_desc: Nine clauses nobody reads, one of them decides the case — cleft sentences to move the focus without raising your voice
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 6 -- Making Every Word Count
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Samuel Rodrigues | Lesson 6 -- Making Every Word Count

listenings.text: Samuel, Diane. I listened to the Aurora call and I want to give you one tool before the next one, because you did something well and something you can do better. What you did well was hold the floor. What cost you ground was the second half, when Karl kept moving the discussion to the revenue figure and you kept following him there. You do not have to raise your voice to bring a conversation back. You move the focus with the sentence itself. Instead of saying the indemnification clause triggered this dispute, say it was the indemnification clause that triggered this dispute. Instead of saying they did not disclose the lien, say what they failed to disclose was the lien. The information is identical. What changes is where the listener has to look, and you did not have to speak faster or louder to do it.

Samuel, Karl again. Quick one, and it is about the back of the document. My team flagged three things in what you would probably call the boilerplate. First, the entire agreement clause is drafted so widely that it may exclude the side letter we signed in June, and that side letter is the only place the cure period is written down. Second, there is no severability provision at all, which for a contract governed by English law is unusual. Third, the notices clause still lists an address in Rio that my company left two years ago. None of this is commercial and none of it is why we are in this deal, but it is exactly the kind of thing that decides a case three years from now. Tell me what you want to do about each one.

matching.title: Match each word to its meaning
defs: the clause saying the contract is the whole deal, and nothing outside it counts
the time you are given to fix a failure before it becomes a breach
the standard clauses at the back that everyone copies and nobody reads
the clause saying where and how a formal message must be sent
an event outside anyone's control that excuses performance
the opening paragraphs that explain why the parties are signing
an amount fixed in advance as compensation for a specific failure
the clause keeping the rest of the contract alive if one part fails

items.situation: The discussion has drifted to revenue. Bring it back to the clause, with a cleft.
tips: It was the indemnification clause that triggered this dispute, not the revenue figure.
It is the entire agreement provision that we need to revisit first.

items.situation: Name the thing that was left out, and make that the point of the sentence.
tips: What they failed to disclose was the lien.
What the side letter contains is the cure period.

items.situation: Say what worries you most, without saying the other side is wrong.
tips: What I find most concerning is the absence of a severability provision.
What concerns me is the scope of the entire agreement clause.

items.situation: He says the boilerplate is not worth the call. Disagree, politely, in one sentence.
tips: I'd push back slightly there: it is the boilerplate that decides the case three years later.
What decides these disputes is usually the clause nobody negotiated.

items.situation: Close: three items, what you will do with each, and a date.
tips: Let me summarise: a side letter carve-out, a severability clause, and a new notices address.
I'll narrow down the three points in writing and come back to you on Thursday.
